Este domingo, una noche inspirada de Nolan Arenado, quien conectó su tercer grand slam de la temporada, fue clave para que Arizona remontara y derrotara 8-4 a los New York Yankees. - LEER MÁS SOBRE: ¡José Ramírez llega a las 1,000 carreras impulsadas! - LEER MÁS SOBRE: ¡Los Atlanta Braves aseguran su boleto a los playoffs! - LEER MÁS SOBRE: New York Yankees 9- 2 Diamondbacks: Resultados y crónica
item.content:encoded:
Los Arizona Diamondbacks volvieron a demostrar que saben reaccionar cuando están contra las cuerdas. Este domingo, una noche inspirada de Nolan Arenado, quien conectó su tercer grand slam de la temporada, fue clave para que Arizona remontara y derrotara 8-4 a los New York Yankees.
- LEER MÁS SOBRE: ¡José Ramírez llega a las 1,000 carreras impulsadas!
- LEER MÁS SOBRE: ¡Los Atlanta Braves aseguran su boleto a los playoffs!
- LEER MÁS SOBRE: New York Yankees 9- 2 Diamondbacks: Resultados y crónica
La jugada que terminó por cambiar el rumbo del encuentro llegó en la quinta entrada. Los Diamondbacks habían conseguido llenar las bases frente al abridor de Nueva York, Will Warren, quien dejó el montículo para darle paso al relevista Brent Headrick.
El pitcher logró retirar a Geraldo Perdomo con un ponche para conseguir el segundo out, pero después vino el descontrol. Headrick otorgó una base por bolas a Corbin Carroll, situación que permitió que Arizona sumara una carrera y dejara las bases listas para Arenado.
Con cuenta de 2-1, el tercera base no perdonó. Arenado encontró el lanzamiento y mandó la pelota por encima de la barda para completar el grand slam y darle la vuelta al partido. Fue el noveno cuadrangular con las bases llenas de su carrera, además de que alcanzó al cubano Yordan Álvarez, de los Houston Astros, como líder de las Grandes Ligas en grand slams durante esta temporada.
Pero el poder ofensivo de Arizona no se limitó a Arenado. Perdomo también tuvo una tarde productiva al conectar un sencillo productor en la primera entrada y posteriormente un triple que llevó otra carrera al plato durante el séptimo episodio.
Los Yankees, por su parte, habían respondido con fuerza en el tercer inning. Heliot Ramos, George Lombard Jr. y Spencer Jones conectaron cuadrangulares consecutivos dentro de esa entrada frente al abridor de Arizona, Corbin Burnes, para mantener con vida a Nueva York.
Sin embargo, la ofensiva neoyorquina se apagó después de ese episodio. El bullpen de Arizona tomó el control y, encabezado por Justin Martínez, consiguió limitar a los Yankees a solamente tres imparables durante las últimas 6 entradas. Martínez se apuntó la victoria, la tercera de su temporada, con marca de 3-0.
Suscríbete al Newsletter de Unanimo y recibe gratis las últimas noticias. Dale click aquí
Arenado héroe de Arizona
Con este triunfo, los Diamondbacks llegaron a 47 victorias conseguidas después de comenzar perdiendo, la cifra más alta de las Grandes Ligas. Arizona continúa además en la pelea con los Philadelphia Phillies por el último boleto de comodín de la Liga Nacional, aunque todavía se encuentra cuatro juegos por detrás cuando restan seis encuentros.
Del otro lado, los Yankees aún conservan posibilidades matemáticas de pelear por el Este de la Liga Americana, aunque necesitan cerrar la temporada con victorias y esperar resultados favorables. Nueva York comenzará el martes una serie de cuatro partidos ante los Tampa Bay Rays, actuales líderes divisionales, en territorio neoyorquino.
Por ahora, Arizona celebra una remontada más en una temporada en la que ha convertido los partidos complicados en una de sus principales características. Y esta vez, el golpe decisivo tuvo nombre y apellido: Nolan Arenado.

item.content:encoded:
HOUSTON -- The frustration oozed out of Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez with every word he spoke to reporters in a hushed clubhouse on Sunday afternoon. It was only moments before that the stoic Alvarez did something he hasn’t done much in his career, speaking up in a players’ meeting following a sweep at the hands of the Braves.
“Basically for us, it was three slaps in the face they gave us right in front of our fans, especially,” Alvarez said through an interpreter. “Just use tomorrow to take it as a reset day and rest, and then the only thing left is to go out there and win the six games we have left.”
Six games on the road -- two against the Mariners in Seattle and four against the A’s in West Sacramento -- are the only games still guaranteed on the Astros’ schedule this season, but they’re hoping for more. Sunday afternoon’s 4-2 loss to the Braves at Daikin Park was Houston’s 10th in its past 14 games, dropping the Astros to 77-79.
“We have six chances to go out there and make the playoffs,” said Alvarez, who is chasing an American League MVP and Triple Crown entering the regular season’s final week.
“Listen, we’ve got to use tomorrow to really gather our thoughts and get a good plan together for the next week,” manager Joe Espada said. “No doubt about it that we need to bounce back and really dig deep and fight, because this series was not what we were expecting.”
Sunday’s script was reminiscent of Saturday’s 6-3 loss, when Braves slugger Ronald Acuna Jr. hit a go-ahead three-run homer in the seventh. The Astros’ led, 1-0, through five innings on Sunday before Bryan King allowed all four batters he faced to reach, capped by MIke Yastrzemski’s three-run homer in the sixth that made it 4-1.
The Astros went 0-for-3 with the bases loaded and did little to back starting pitcher Hunter Brown, who struck out 10 batters in five scoreless innings. Brown also walked three batters and was pulled after throwing 98 pitches, but Houston’s battered bullpen couldn’t hold the lead for the second game in a row.
“We can still make a big push here,” Brown said. “We’re right in it. We’re not dead yet. That’s what we’re going to do, give it our all these last six games and find out where we are after that.”
Alvarez refused to divulge what was said in his speech or who else spoke up, but outfielder Taylor Trammell said his message carried weight.
“He doesn’t talk much and when he speaks, there’s a presence,” Trammell said. “This was not a ‘hoorah’ or anything like that. It’s just like, ‘Hey guys, Easy. Just be easy with it,’ and hearing it from him, it means something. You see the way he’s played all year and you can’t tell me there hasn’t been any nicks or bangs for him. And he’s going out there every single day and being the best hitter in the game right now. That’s what he’s doing. And so when he says something and he talks, you listen.”
Veteran first baseman Christian Walker said Alvarez’s speech stressed a sense of urgency facing the Astros, who were knocked out of first place on Saturday for the first time since late July. Houston missed the postseason by one game last year, ending its run of eight consecutive playoff appearances.
Alvarez challenged his teammates to get back to October.
“Everybody is going to receive things differently, but younger guys who haven’t been to the postseason, it feels like there’s a lot of pressure right now, and there is,” Walker said. “And that’s a good thing, because we played ourselves into a spot to be competitive. I think any time a vet can address the team, especially somebody like Yordan, if nothing else, for everybody to feel the calmness he brings to the table. That can be helpful.”
The Mariners (73-83), whose slim playoff hopes are still alive, would love nothing more to spoil it for the Astros, who are 2-9 against Seattle. Houston ends the season playing in a Minor League ballpark in West Sacramento that can be about as unpredictable as it gets and wants to leave nothing to chance.
“These next two teams have nothing to lose,” Walker said. “Their goal is to knock us out. I’ve been on teams where we’ve been in that position before and it can be a dangerous spot. I think it’s a good reminder to come into these cities with a fire and a sense of urgency, and prepare to come in and win some baseball games.”

item.content:encoded:
Yordan Alvarez Gives Bold Quote, Calls Team Meeting as Astros Fall in MLB Playoff Standings
Yordan Alvarez was not pleased after the Houston Astros were swept by the Atlanta Braves over the weekend, leaving them a game behind the Texas Rangers in the AL West with just six games remaining.
The superstar slugger told reporters he called a team meeting following Sunday's 4-2 loss:
Alvarez, 29, has more than done his part this season, hitting .313 with 40 homers, 99 RBI, 98 runs and a 1.027 OPS. He's likely going to be the AL MVP, though it likely won't mean nearly as much if the Astros—who have lost 10 of their last 14 games—fail to reach the postseason.
They will have two games remaining against the Seattle Mariners and four against the Athletics to salvage the season. The Rangers will finish with three games against the New York Mets and three games against the Minnesota Twins.

item.dc:creator: Theo DeRosa
item.description: One well-timed hot streak from a star player can be all a team needs to go on a big run. item.content:encoded:
One well-timed hot streak from a star player can be all a team needs to go on a big run.
While many key contributors struggled in the first half of 2026, several have picked it up big time since the All-Star break, lifting their clubs to late-season success.
Here are 10 players -- five hitters and five pitchers -- who have turned things around in the second half.
All stats are through Saturday's games unless otherwise specified.
Hitters
Alex Bregman, Cubs
For as good as National League MVP Award favorite Pete Crow-Armstrong has been lately, it’s actually Bregman who entered Saturday leading all qualifying hitters with a 168 wRC+ in the second half. The third baseman has a .298/.376/.609 slash line since the All-Star break, with his 17 second-half homers tied for fourth most in MLB.
Batting just .241 with nine home runs and a .695 OPS prior to the break, Bregman hadn’t exactly been meeting expectations after signing a five-year, $175 million deal with the Cubs. Now, though, he is up to 5.1 FanGraphs WAR, his highest total since 2022 (5.4). He’s been a big reason the Cubs are currently on track to host an NL Wild Card Series at Wrigley Field, and he will be a key bat in the middle of Chicago’s lineup in the postseason.
Steven Kwan, Guardians
With this week’s series win over the White Sox, the Guardians have surged into first place in the AL Central, in large part thanks to their leadoff hitter’s resurgence. In addition to his strong defense in left field -- Kwan has won four straight AL Gold Gloves in left to begin his career -- Kwan has been on fire at the plate.
After a disappointing first-half slash line of .225/.332/.282, including a .188 batting average in May, Kwan ranks second among qualifiers with a .347 average and is tied with Yordan Alvarez for first with a .435 on-base percentage in the second half. He has been setting the table admirably for a Cleveland club not getting as much as usual from third baseman José Ramírez (94 wRC+) and could help the Guardians secure not only the division title but a key first-round bye.
Jackson Merrill, Padres
Merrill took a step back in 2025 after finishing second to the Pirates’ Paul Skenes in 2024 NL Rookie of the Year Award voting, and the Padres center fielder appeared headed for further regression based on early returns in 2026. Merrill’s OPS was below .600 in late May as San Diego scuffled offensively, and he took a .219/.278/.350 slash line into the break.
Since then, Merrill has been a major reason why the Padres have a 38-21 (.644) record in the second half, tied with the Brewers for the best in the NL. He’s hitting .312 with 16 home runs, 48 RBIs and a .944 OPS in 59 games in the second half while playing standout defense in center. Merrill’s ability to recapture his rookie form has given the Padres a fighting chance to host a Wild Card Series, and he’ll be a key middle-of-the-order bat for the club.
George Springer, Blue Jays
Springer improved his OPS by nearly 300 points from 2024 to 2025, slashing .309/.399/.560 and finishing seventh in AL MVP balloting as Toronto fell just short of a World Series title. But the veteran’s numbers fell off again early in 2026, especially after Springer returned from a stint on the injured list for a left big toe fracture. He hit just .218 with a .677 OPS before the All-Star break, a period of rest that seemed to help considerably.
Springer recorded multiple hits in five of his first nine second-half games, finishing July with an .878 OPS, before batting .321 with an .858 OPS in August. While he has slowed a bit in September, battling multiple injuries, he has clearly found his footing at the plate. It might not be enough to drag a Blue Jays team dealing with a host of pitching injuries and a down year from Vladimir Guerrero Jr. to the postseason, but Toronto -- three games out of an AL Wild Card spot -- still has a chance.
Fernando Tatis Jr., Padres
While Merrill’s turnaround has been integral to the Padres’ second-half surge, Tatis’ production out of the leadoff spot has perhaps been even more important. The three-time All-Star began the season by scorching the baseball into the ground, going 55 games before hitting his first home run of the year on May 30.
The second half brought on a true power surge for Tatis, who homered three times in his first four games after the All-Star break and is now up to 24 dingers on the season. Entering Saturday, his 167 wRC+ in the second half was second in MLB, behind only Bregman. Tatis has raised his season OPS to .819 and has given the Padres a dangerous option at leadoff down the stretch.
Pitchers
Brayan Bello, Red Sox
Bello has turned the page on a dismal start to the season. The right-hander, coming off a 3.35 ERA as a starter in 2025, had a 9.00 ERA in his first six starts of 2026 and was moved to a bulk-relief role. Still, Bello took a 6.06 ERA into the All-Star break as the Red Sox finally began to heat up, winning nine straight games to end the first half and extending the streak to a franchise record-tying 15.
Bello has continued to impress for Boston, earning the start on Saturday and baffling the Rays over eight innings of one-run ball with 11 strikeouts. In the midst of a statistically unprecedented season, he’s found something that works, which has been crucial for a Red Sox team that has surged into postseason position and appears headed for another clash with the Yankees in the AL Wild Card Series.
Robert Gasser, Brewers
Tommy John surgery in June 2024 cut short Gasser’s promising rookie season, but he returned to make two solid starts at the tail end of 2025. The left-hander couldn’t sustain that success early in 2026, taking a 5.24 ERA into the All-Star break after being tagged for seven runs in three innings in his final first-half start.
Since then, Gasser has a 3.00 ERA in 57 innings of work after holding the Orioles scoreless over seven excellent innings on Saturday in Baltimore. In his first four September outings, including two against the Cubs, he has allowed just four earned runs across 21 innings pitched. With Brandon Woodruff’s 2026 return questionable and Kyle Harrison struggling mightily, Gasser’s improvement has made him an important arm for a Milwaukee team fighting to secure the NL’s No. 1 seed.
Tyler Mahle, Braves
Mahle owned a 5.13 ERA through his first 18 starts of 2026 for the Giants, but the Braves saw something in the veteran right-hander. Atlanta acquired Mahle ahead of the Trade Deadline for righty reliever Anthony Molina in a move that has paid considerable dividends for the Braves’ battered rotation.
Mahle has allowed only seven earned runs in eight starts for Atlanta, completing six or more innings in all but one of those outings. His 1.28 ERA in that span is the third best among all pitchers (min. 40 innings), and he’s been an excellent complement to ace lefty Chris Sale atop the Braves rotation. With Spencer Strider, Spencer Schwellenbach, Bryce Elder, Reynaldo López and Hurston Waldrep all on the injured list, Mahle has not only covered important innings but has been remarkably effective.
Aaron Nola, Phillies
Nola had an ERA above 6 in an injury-marred 2025 season, and his 2026 looked to be more of the same. The usually dependable right-hander gave up 20 home runs in the first half alone, tied for the fifth most in MLB, and headed into the All-Star break with a 5.75 ERA.
Since then, Nola has returned to near-vintage form for the Phillies, who have also gotten strong second halves from lefty Jesús Luzardo (currently on the injured list with left shoulder inflammation) and rookie righty Andrew Painter. After Thursday’s excellent start against the Mets, Nola has a 2.78 ERA in the second half, striking out 67 in 71 1/3 innings despite giving up 14 more home runs in just 12 starts. If he can limit the long balls, he could be at least an adequate replacement for Luzardo if the southpaw cannot return for the start of the postseason.
Brandon Pfaadt, D-backs
Pfaadt hasn’t quite lived up to his billing as a former top prospect just yet, but he’s shown flashes, such as his success against the Dodgers and Phillies during the D-backs’ 2023 World Series run. The righty's recent results have been quite encouraging, too: Pfaadt has a 3.01 ERA in the second half, including a run of 27 2/3 scoreless innings across four starts from July 28-Aug. 14. 
Optioned to Triple-A Reno in June after a poor start to the year, Pfaadt now has the chance to help pitch the D-backs into the playoffs, which might be difficult in an NL Wild Card race featuring the Cubs, Phillies and Padres. Pfaadt is lined up to start during Arizona’s final series of the season, a pivotal three-game set in San Diego from Sept. 25-27, and his outing could determine the D-backs’ postseason fate.

item.content:encoded:
Conecta Isaac Paredes su jonrón número 22, pero los Astros pierden liderato de su división
El hermosillense esta a nueve cuandrangulares de su récord en Grandes Ligas
Isaac Paredes conectó este sábado su cuadrangular número 22 en la presente campaña de MLB, aunque no fue suficiente para evitar que los Astros de Houston cayeran por 6-3 ante los Bravos de Atlanta y cayeran al segundo lugar en la División Oeste de la Liga Americana.
El tablazo del hermosillense llegó en el cierre de la primera entrada, ante el abridor Grant Holmes, quien había dominado a Jeremy Peña y a Yordan Álvarez iniciando esa tanda.
Paredes remolcó una segunda anotación en la tercera baja, con un sencillo al jardín derecho que fue suficiente para impulsar a Peña después después que este último había conectado un triple.
El mexicano también anotó dos carreras, una vez que en el octavo episodio negoció una base por bolas y más tarde fue mandado al plato con doblete de Yainer Díaz.
Con siete campañas de experiencia en Grandes Ligas, la presente ya es la segunda mejor en términos de cuadrangulares para el sonorense, solo por detrás de los 31 conseguidos en 2023 con los Rays de Tampa Bay.
Ese jonrón también lo acercó a 10 del récord que ostenta Aurelio Rodríguez (124), el tercer jugador nacido en México con más cuadrangulares en Ligas Mayores. Vinicio Castilla (320) y Jorge Orta (130) encabezan la lista.
A los Astros de Houston les restan siete encuentros en la temporada regular, por lo que su marca podría incrementarse todavía más de aquí al próximo domingo 27 de septiembre.

item.content:encoded:
Since he hit Seth Lugo’s fastball, Yordan Alvarez knew that ball was out of the park. The hit came off at 107.2 mph and landed 385 feet into right field, right in the second-level seats at Daikin Park to give Houston a 4-1 lead over the Kansas City Royals earlier this week.
Thus continued Alvarez's pursuit of the Triple Crown—the last one was won by Miguel Cabrera in 2012 with the Detroit Tigers in the American League—, hitting his 40th home run of the season to join a select club in the history of the Astros and players born in Cuba.
He became just the fifth player in Astros history to reach that mark:
• Jeff Bagwell — 47 (2000), 43 (1997), 42 (1999)
• Lance Berkman — 45 (2006), 42 (2002)
• Richard Hidalgo — 44 (2000)
• Alex Bregman — 41 (2019)
• Yordan Alvarez — 40 (2026)
The Hall of Fame member, Jeff Bagwell, was the first Houston hitter to hit 40 or more home runs in a season, when he achieved the feat with 43 home runs in 1997, at 29 years old. In his entire career, he finished recording three similar seasons (1997, 1999 and 2000).
The 47 home runs he hit in the 2000 season remained marked as the most in club history. Richard Hidalgo (44 HR in 2000) and Alex Bregman (41 in 2019) have been the youngest hitters to enter the club, both at 25 years old. But this season, he has made the difference in an unprecedented season for a 40-home-run hitter who has worn the Astros uniform, as he leads the league with an offensive line of .311/.429/.598, 1.027 OPS, 189 OPS+, 319 total bases, 103 walks and 32 intentional walks.
After going through a slump in his home run production, with only five in the last 40 games, Alvarez has heated up again with a pair of home runs in his last 10 at-bats, both in the series that Houston won 2-1 against the Royals. Now he is one home run away from tying Tampa Bay Rays third baseman Junior Caminero, who leads the American League with 41, and three RBIs away from reaching Pete Alonso (102).
Houston has eight games remaining to finish the regular season, two more against the Atlanta Braves at home, a two-game road trip against the Seattle Mariners and four against the Athletics.
Another Chapter of Glory Among Cuban Hitters
Alvarez also joined the list of only four Cuban-born hitters who have hit at least 40 home runs in the Majors. The legendary Cooperstown Hall of Fame member, Tony Pérez, was the first Cuban-born hitter to hit at least 40 home runs in a season, when he reached the milestone in the 1970 season with the Cincinnati Reds’ “Big Red Machine.”
Eighteen years later, José Canseco appears on the historical list, at just 23 years old, in his historic 40-40 season (42 home runs and 40 stolen bases), wearing the Oakland Athletics uniform in 1988.
Canseco entered the club four times, repeating the feat with 41 home runs in 1991 and 46 in 1998. Another who reached the milestone was Rafael Palmeiro, who leads the group of Cuban hitters with four 40-home-run seasons (1998-1999 and 2000 and 2002). Seventeen years later, Jorge Soler hit 48 home runs with the Royals and took ownership of the record for Cubans in a single season, leaving behind Palmeiro’s 47-home-run seasons in 1999 and 2001.
For the first time in the club, Alvarez can go much farther if he manages to regain his home run pace in these last nine games. Before reaching the August and September stretch, his worst month in production had been June when he hit six home runs in 26 games. However, as we saw before, he has been able to take only five balls out of the park since August 1 until now, and that has made the race against Caminero become much more attractive.
Alvarez still has the possibility of reaching a Triple Crown by leading all three offensive categories in all of MLB, a feat that no hitter has accomplished since Mickey Mantle with the New York Yankees in 1956 (.353 BA, 52 HR, 130 RBI).
Yirsandy is a baseball writer specializing in MLB coverage with experience across multiple teams and storylines. He currently writes for Diamond Centric, where he covers the New York Mets, San Diego Padres, Chicago Cubs, Milwaukee Brewers, and Kansas City Royals. My work focuses on game coverage, player analysis, and storytelling that connects performance with context. My Substack has also been an important part of my writing development, where I’ve built much of my baseball coverage and storytelling voice over time. I’m passionate about combining reporting, research, and thoughtful analysis to produce engaging baseball content for readers.

item.content:encoded:
Yordan Alvarez has been the American League's best hitter in 2026. But is that enough for him to be crowned AL MVP? The Astros' designated hitter has one week left to hold off young Rays superstar Junior Caminero, who has made a surge for the award in recent weeks.
There's no denying that the Astros' slugger has had a monster season, hitting .311 with 40 homers and 99 RBI in 149 games entering Friday. He currently leads the AL in on-base percentage (.429), slugging (.598) and OPS (1.027). And he has stayed healthy and played in all but four of Houston's games, allowing him to put together a remarkable season.
When it comes to winning MVP, the numbers are critically important, and the narrative of the season plays a part as well. But an often overlooked aspect of award voting, particularly for MVP, is historical precedent.
Alvarez is a primary designated hitter, and prior to Shohei Ohtani's historic 50/50 season in 2024, in which he did not pitch but won NL MVP, no primary DH had ever won the MVP Award. Ohtani in 2024 is still the only DH to do it, given that in his other MVP seasons, he also pitched.
Considering his singular status as a two-way player, Ohtani is the exception to this rule. Besides him, no full-time designated hitter has ever won MVP. In fact, since 2000, only six designated hitters have finished in the top five of MVP voting. That list includes Frank Thomas (second in 2000, fourth in 2006), David Ortiz (fifth in 2003, fourth in 2004, second in 2005, third in 2006, fourth in 2007), Travis Hafner (fifth in 2005), J.D. Martinez (fourth in 2018), Marcell Ozuna (fourth in 2024) and Kyle Schwarber (second in 2025). Alvarez finished third in 2022 while splitting time between DH and outfield.
Among designated hitters since 1995, here are five of the top seasons comparable to Alvarez's 2026 and where they finished in MVP balloting:
- Edgar Martinez, 1995: .356/.479/.628, 182 H, 29 HR, 113 RBI, 182 wRC+, 7.0 fWAR — third
- Frank Thomas, 2000: .328/.436/.625, 191 H, 43 HR, 143 RBI, 160 wRC+, 5.9 fWAR — second
- David Ortiz, 2005: .300/.397/.604, 180 H, 47 HR, 148 RBI, 157 wRC+, 5.3 fWAR — second
- David Ortiz, 2007: .332/.445/.621, 182 H, 35 HR, 117 RBI, 175 wRC+, 6.3 fWAR — fourth
- J.D. Martinez, 2018: .330/.402/.629, 188 H, 43 HR, 130 RBI, 170 wRC+, 5.8 fWAR — fourth
- Yordan Alvarez, 2026: 311/.429/.598, 166 H, 40 HR, 99 RBI, 177 wRC+, 6.2 fWAR — ?
When you look at what Alvarez has accomplished this season, his numbers with eight games to play are right in line with those of his elite DH contemporaries. But if designated hitters who put up similar seasons weren't able to win MVP, will the Astros' slugger be able to reverse that trend?
Short of playing a defensive position, Alvarez has done everything he can to hold off Caminero, but the Rays' third baseman has made a push over the past month. The 23-year-old, who has earned the title of best player on the AL's best team, is slashing .277/.363/.532 with 41 home runs and 96 RBI this season. Although he rates out poorly defensively, Caminero has appeared in 151 games and counting at the hot corner. Plus, he delivered his potential MVP moment with a walk-off homer to clinch a playoff berth for the Rays.
One of the things working against Alvarez is the fact that, after being on pace to do so for most of the season, he is now unlikely to win the AL Triple Crown. Entering Friday, he's tied with Tampa Bay's Chandler Simpson for the league lead in batting average, he's second to Caminero in home runs, and he's second in RBI behind Baltimore's Pete Alonso.
Recent history tells us that a historic season, like Ohtani's 50/50 season in 2024 or Aaron Judge's AL-record 61 home runs in 2022, can provide the narrative juice to pave the way to MVP, making the Triple Crown Alvarez's best path to the award this year. Only Miguel Cabrera in 2012 has accomplished that feat in the past 60 years. Without the Triple Crown, it'll likely be tougher for Alvarez to sway voters.
Another thing that's likely hurting Alvarez's case is how poorly the Astros have played in 2026. They might be one of the worst division winners in MLB history, or they could still miss the postseason completely. That said, there's precedent for this in recent MVP voting, as Bryce Harper won the 2021 NL MVP Award on an 82-80 Phillies team that missed the postseason.
Over the past six seasons, the AL MVP Award has been dominated by Ohtani and Judge, with very little argument in the years they've won. But this season, with Alvarez and Caminero, voters will be selecting a new winner, and they'll have to decide what's most important in determining most valuable.
For the Astros' slugger, we'll wait to see if a nearly historic season by a designated hitter can be enough.

item.content:encoded:
The Triple Crown in the baseball world is a bit of an old-school feat, but it is a feat that very rarely happens these days, nonetheless. No hitter has won a Triple Crown since Miguel Cabrera pulled it off in 2012. Cabrera's feat was the first since 1967. A Triple Crown is leading your respective league in batting average, home runs and RBI. As noted, it's a bit old school because batting average isn't the most preferred rate stat and people have also shifted attention away from RBI.
Still, it's really cool to track when someone is close, and Astros outfielder and AL MVP frontrunner Yordan Alvarez has a real shot as the 2026 season winds down.
Heading into the penultimate weekend of the 2026 MLB season, here are the leaderboards, with Alvarez sitting in the top two of each category.
AL batting average leaders
1. Yordan Alvarez, Astros: .311 (.311444)
2. Chandler Simpson, Rays: .311 (.310661)
3. Yandy Díaz, Rays: .295
AL home run runs
1. Junior Caminero, Rays, 41
2. Yordan Alvarez, Astros, 40
3. Ben Rice, Yankees, 38
4. Pete Alonso, Orioles, 37
AL RBI leaders
1. Pete Alonso, Orioles, 102
2. Yordan Alvarez, Astros, 99
3. Junior Caminero, Rays, 96
4. Jo Adell, Guardians, 92
5. Ben Rice, Yankees, 92
As illustrated, all are tight races. It's possible Alvarez ends up leading the AL in none of the three categories, but he's right on the precipice of having a lead in all three.
Coincidentally, the last six Triple Crown winners in MLB have all been on the AL side. No National League player has won the Triple Crown since Hall of Famer Joe "Ducky" Medwick in 1937. Since then, the AL has seen Ted Williams (1942 and 1947), Mickey Mantle (1956), Frank Robinson (1966), Carl Yastrzemski (1967) and Miguel Cabrera (2012) pull it off.
No Astros player has ever won the Triple Crown.
Yordan Alvarez Triple Crown prediction
Could Alvarez become the first? The Astros -- who are clinging to the lead in the AL West -- and Alvarez have nine games remaining: they host the Braves for a three-game set this weekend before closing the regular season with a six-game road trip in Seattle (two games) and Sacramento (four games)
The two games in Seattle bring a difficult ballpark, but with three home games and finishing with four in Sacramento's Sutter Health Park, the conditions seem ripe for a strong finish. I'll predict that he gets the job done and wins the Triple Crown.

item.title: [NBC Sports] The 2026 MLB Season from A to Z: Yordan Alvarez, PCA, Jacob Misiorowski and more

item.content:encoded:
Many fans rely on numbers to tell the story of a baseball season. For 2026, I’m going with letters. Here’s the story of the regular season from A to Z.

A: Yordan Alvarez: He’s the only qualifier in baseball with an OBP of over .400. He’s leading the American League in batting, on-base, slugging, OPS, and walks. Where would Joe Espada’s Astros be without him? Yordan is still the favorite to win the American League MVP, despite his numbers falling off a bit down the stretch.
B: Bryan Baker: Tampa Bay scored 698 runs and allowed 618 in games through September 17. That would give them a record of 84-68 according to the Pythagorean Theorem. But they were 93-59, nine games better. Credit in part goes to their closer Baker, leading the league with 40 saves this season..
C: Pete Crow-Armstrong: When the Cubs suffered through a 10-game losing streak in May, Pete batted just .161 (5-36 AB) in those 10 games. In games through September 17, PCA in 85 Cubs victories: .357/.442/.740. He scored 89 runs in 85 Cubs wins. The NL MVP by a mile. You cannot tell the story of the 2026 season without talking about Pete Crow-Armstrong.
D: Jacob deGrom: On September 10, deGrom started against the Mariners in Seattle. In six innings, he faced just 19 batters, one over the minimum. He struck out 12, gave up one hit, walked none, and didn’t allow a run. He left the game with Texas leading by three runs. The bullpen flushed away the lead and Texas wound up losing the game. The story of deGrom’s career. Jacob is historically significant. He has started 277 games in his career, and three of his top 10 (ranked by Pitchers’ Game Score) have come in 2026.
E: Errors: There’s only been one season EVER with fewer errors per game than 2026. Of course, that would be 2025. No pitcher has made more than four errors this season. In 1969, Jim Kaat won a Gold Glove, despite making eight errors (tied for the MLB lead with Boston’s Ray Culp among pitchers). Gold Gloves were all reputation in those days. In fact, Kaat’s longtime Minnesota teammate, Zoilo Versalles, won a Gold Glove in 1965 despite making 39 errors!
F: Freddie Freeman: Freeman has hit 32 doubles this year and 579 in his career. Is 579 doubles a lot? Well, that’s 90 more than the next-closest active player, Paul Goldschmidt. And when Freddie legs out his 600th, he’ll become only the 19th player with at least 600 doubles. He’s a little more than a season away from passing both Hank Aaron (624) and Barry Bonds (601).
G: Vladimir Guerrero Jr.: Vlad Jr. hit a home run every 25 at-bats in 2025. He’s hit a home run every 58 at-bats in 2026. He didn’t hit his first home run at home this year until Toronto’s 75th home game. He had gone 84 straight home games without a homer.
H: Bryce Harper: In March, Harper hit a two-run game-tying homer in the 8th inning of the WBC Finals. This season, his wRC+ (139) has been one of the top dozen in the majors. In October, can he lead the Phillies to his first World Series championship?
I: Raisel Iglesias: The Braves have spent all season in first place, and Iglesias is a big part of that. In the last 10 years (2017-2026) only one player (Kenley Jansen) has more saves than Iglesias. He’s 33-for-36 in save chances this year for the Braves. But here’s the thing: over the last five years, he’s saved 130 games for the Braves, but only one in the postseason. That has to change.
J: Aaron Judge: #99 missed 99 days (84 games) this season with a rib injury, but the three-time MVP came back in mid-September with enough time to get his timing back at the plate. Yankees fans will have to hope that the leg tightness isn’t a big deal.
K: Steven Kwan: There hasn’t been a hotter hitter in the American League since the start of July. Kwan is batting .350 since July 1, and .351 since the All-Star break. The Guardians have needed every bit of his offense, as José Ramírez has not been the same since returning from his broken left hamate bone.
L: Brandon Lowe: In his first season with Pittsburgh, Lowe has hit a career best 30 homers and has an OPS over .800. The Pirates offense was one of the big stories of the first half of the 2026 season, and Lowe was a big reason why. In the second half, injuries to Oneil Cruz and Ryan O’Hearn have sunk the Bucs but the offense was fun while it lasted.
M: Jacob Misiorowski: Milwaukee has the best record in baseball, and he’s a big reason why. Has any Brewers pitcher ever had a better season than the 24-year-old ace? Sorry, fans of Teddy Higuera. The answer is no. “The Miz” leads the majors in strikeouts (243). He leads the majors in ERA (1.89). He’s striking out more than 13 batters per nine innings! Misiorowski has had 1,053 pitches this season over 100.0 mph. No one else in pitch tracking era (2008-present) has had a season of 1,000 or more.
N: No-Hitters: On May 25, three Astros pitchers Tatsuya Imai (6 IP), Steven Okert (1 IP), and Alimber Santa (2 IP) combined to complete the Astros’ fifth combined no-hitter in franchise history. No one pitcher has completed a no-hitter since Blake Snell did it in August of 2024 for the Giants.
O: Shohei Ohtani: There are two players whose last name starts with “O” with more homers than Ohtani this season: Matt Olson and Kazuma Okamoto. But Ohtani made 14 brilliant starts (1.79 ERA) and his wRC+ of 142 is in the top 10 in the game.
P: Salvador Perez: The 36-year-old put up nearly 600 at-bats this season. And while most of them came as a DH or 1B, he did start 44 games behind the plate. In his 15-year career, he’s caught 1,427 games (1,396 starts) and nearly 12,000 innings.
Q: Quick games: On September 7, in an afternoon game at Citizens Bank Park, the Phillies beat the Braves 1-0 in a game that took 1:51 to play. On June 16 at Dodger Stadium, the Dodgers defeated the Rays 1-0 in a game that took 1:52 to complete. And in early April, the Royals defeated the White Sox in games on April 10 and 11 that lasted in 1:54 and 1:55, respectively. Thank you, pitch clock.
R: Eduardo Rodriguez: The Diamondbacks have won 22 of E-Rod’s first 30 starts. Talk about valuable! He has a 2.62 ERA this season (it was 5.04 and 5.02 in the two previous seasons). This is his best year since 2019.
S: Cam Schlittler: Is he the AL MVP, or just the AL Cy Young? The Yankees won 20 of his 31 starts. The Yankees don’t need a lot of offense when he takes the mound. He has a 1.14 ERA in 16 road starts this season! Since earned runs became official in both leagues in 1913, Schlittler’s 1.14 road ERA is the fourth best (minimum 15 road starts). The top three: Bob Gibson in 1968 (0.81 ERA); Walter Johnson in 1913 (1.06 ERA); and Greg Maddux in 1995 (1.12 ERA).
T: Bruce Turang: What a player! His OPS has gone up in each of his first four seasons. He’s now a 20 HR/20 SB/100 runs/100 RBI player. The Brewers need him to improve his performance in last year’s NLCS vs. the Dodgers, when he went 1-for-15 (.067).
U: Uncle Charlie (curveball): The curveball is heading toward extinction, much like individual no-hitters. Curveballs have only accounted for 6.4% of pitches this season, the second lowest rate since first tracked in 2008 (2024: 6.1%). That’s pure curves, not including slow curves or knuckle-curves. Want to know which pitcher has thrown the most curveballs (including knuckle and slow curves) this year? Philadelphia’s Aaron Nola, at 942.
V: Miguel Vargas: The White Sox have been one of the best stories this year, and we could have given the “V” to manager Max Venable. But Vargas’ 31 home runs and stealing 19 bases in 21 attempts makes him the choice. Vargas has a 4.7 WAR this season, up from 1.9 last year.
W: Willson and Wilyer, the heart of the Boston lineup. Right fielder Wilyer Abreu leads the American League with 36 doubles. He also leads the AL in outfield assists with 12. Willson Contreras has an OPS of .905, second in AL to Alvarez, even ahead of Rays slugger Junior Caminero. Remember, Boston was 14 games under .500 as late as June 24. And then the season turned around.
X: Xander Bogaerts: The Padres have played well down the stretch and now appear likely to reach the postseason. And X-Man has contributed, stealing 21 bases in 22 attempts this year. It’s no fluke, either. He stole 20 of 22 last season. In his four seasons with the Padres, he has stolen 73 bases in 81 attempts. That’s efficiency.
Y: Yoshinobu Yamamoto: The Dodgers’ Yoshinobu Yamamoto has a 1.98 ERA in 10 starts after the All-Star break. He’s probably the key to the Dodgers’ chances of completing a three-peat. Who can forget what he did last October, when he went 5-1, with a 1.45 ERA in 37.1 postseason innings.
Z: Zack Wheeler: From July 21 through August 24, Wheeler had a stretch of seven starts that saw him give up 26 runs (25 earned) in 31.1 innings (7.18 ERA). He was terrific in the first half and recaptured his form down the stretch. If the Phillies are going to go deep into October, they’ll need Wheeler (and their other two aces) to be at the top of their game.
Editors’ Note: Elliott Kalb - dubbed “Mr. Stats” decades ago by Marv Albert and Bob Costas - is the former Senior Editorial Director at MLB Network and a longtime contributor of research and information to NBC Sports’ telecasts.
